result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Answer A makes one clear choice (Source Sans 3, OFL), ties it to the readers' devices, and gives ready-to-use self-hosted CSS that ends in a generic family, plus an honest warning that very old Android may not support variable fonts. Answer B is a little stronger on print, giving sizes for body text and warnings, but it is less decisive and puts Charter in a stack without saying it can't be assumed on Windows or Android. Both only suggest testing with the font blocked; neither asks for a check on an old phone, a library computer or a test print. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers recommend free, legible, open-licensed families and give self-hosting advice with fallback stacks that end in a generic family. B is more concrete. It commits to one pick, gives working @font-face CSS, warns that variable fonts may not work on very old Android, and explains how to embed fonts so the PDF handout matches the web pages. Neither answer explicitly suggests testing on an old phone, a library PC or a test print beyond loading the page with the font blocked, and B's stack includes Helvetica Neue without noting that it won't be on those machines.
